text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x) ::: Pets are allowed in building x.
RequiresDeposit(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in building x.
EqualDeposit(x) ::: The security deposit in building x is equal to one month's rent.
MoreDeposit(x) ::: The security deposit in building x is more than one month's rent.
Owns(tom, fluffy) ::: Tom owns the cat Fluffy.
Pet(x) ::: x is a pet.
ManagedBuilding(x) ::: x is a managed building.
RentAmount(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at building x is y dollars.
RentWithPet(tom) ::: Tom will rent an apartment if he is allowed to move in with his pet.
DepositAmount(x, y) ::: The security deposit at building x is y dollars.

Premises:
∃x (ManagedBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (RequiresDeposit(x) → ∃y (EqualDeposit(y) ∨ MoreDeposit(y))) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building, and it can be either equal to or more than one month's rent.
Owns(tom, fluffy) ∧ Pet(fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat, and cats are pets.
RentAmount(oliveGarden, 2000) ∧ ManagedBuilding(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building with a monthly rent of $2000.
RentWithPet(tom) ↔ (Allowed(oliveGarden) ∧ DepositAmount(oliveGarden, noMoreThan1500)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
2000 > 1500 ::: $2000 is more than $1500.

Conclusion:
DepositAmount(oliveGarden, 2000) ∨ MoreDeposit(oliveGarden) ::: The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more.
